tasks.short: Analyze file signatures to verify files and discover hidden files.

steps.what: Verify the authorized forensic image and choose file signature analysis scope
Configure file signature searches and inspect forensic tool classification results
Examine mismatched signatures and hidden-file candidates against original bytes and file structures
Document file signature findings with evidence offsets and limitations
Approve the final file signature findings and supporting evidence references
Commit the approved signature findings to the forensic case record

tasks.design: Configure native mismatch views in the forensic-analysis category of {OTHER}, preserving the source image. Reuse evidence offsets and tool versions in the findings draft, with human byte-level interpretation and a final case-record gate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Analysts repeat searches and copy evidence references between examination and case notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exception filters and evidence-linked exports reduce navigation and transcription.
tasks.still_hard: A signature mismatch may reflect corruption, an embedded object or deliberate concealment.
tasks.human_edge: Explain what the bytes establish and what they cannot establish.
tasks.altitude: Less navigation and reference copying; evidential interpretation is unchanged.

reach.task: Relate suspicious file structures to intrusion evidence

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: forensic tools can compare file signatures, expose mismatches and export evidence references; those matches do not prove concealment.

assumptions: Boundary begins with an acquired, authorized forensic image and ends with recorded findings. Acquisition effort is outside this task; neither scanning runtime nor existing classification automation earns savings. Shares are provisional.
Acquisition staff supply image ID, hash, source-media identity and custody manifest. s1 verifies these and chooses scope; missing integrity or authority stops work.

The forensic tool produces file path or inode, byte offset, claimed extension, detected signature, tool version and image hash. s2 checks coverage and manually examines unrecognized formats; s3 retains all interpretation.

First test native mismatch filters and export templates. s4 saves only copying existing evidence references, not writing conclusions. The final document and attachments exist before s5; revisions void the s6 gate.
research_questions: Can exception views reduce navigation without hiding uncommon or embedded formats?

already_counted.description: Approve final signature findings and references

incremental.description: Validate signature definitions and export compatibility

approvals.approved_version: Complete findings revision and referenced evidence snapshot approved in s5; any change requires reapproval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes nine navigation, two reference-copying and two record-entry hours less two upkeep. Low assumes existing exception views and reference exports already remove the first two gains; final record entry offsets upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recover data or decrypt seized data.

steps.what: Assess seized data integrity, encryption and authorized recovery scope
Configure forensic recovery methods and authorized decryption inputs on working copies
Supervise data recovery or decryption and adapt to damaged or unsupported structures
Validate recovered data integrity and document recovery methods and limitations
Approve the final recovered-data package for the evidence repository
Commit the approved recovered data and provenance to the evidence repository

tasks.design: Reuse validated recovery profiles in the forensic-recovery category of {OTHER}. The analyst selects methods, supervises working-copy recovery and validates the resulting package before a gated evidence-repository commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supported media types require repeated job settings and package registration.
tasks.enabler_now: Native recovery profiles and repository import can reduce repeated handling, without breaking encryption.
tasks.still_hard: Unavailable keys, damaged media and unsupported formats may prevent recovery entirely.
tasks.human_edge: Choose defensible recovery methods and distinguish valid content from plausible corrupted output.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in repeated setup; recovery expertise and success limits remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: forensic recovery tools support saved job profiles and repository exports; they cannot guarantee decryption without suitable keys or viable recovery methods.

assumptions: Boundary excludes seizure and initial imaging, but includes actual analyst supervision, validation and evidence registration. s3 measures active labour only, not long unattended recovery or password-search runtime. Shares are provisional.

Acquisition staff provide image hash, media ID, custody and authority. An authorized custodian supplies any available keys; the design does not assume keys exist or create extra credential collection work for another role.

s1 determines format, damage, authorized scope and viable methods. s2 manually chooses parameters and records source image, tool version and output location; reuse affects repeated settings only. Unsupported jobs remain manual.

s4 produces package hash, source link, method log and limitations during retained validation time. Test native profiles and import first. Original evidence is never overwritten; s6 writes only the approved package and invalidates approval on changed contents.
research_questions: Is repeated setup large enough to cover profile validation overhead on this case mix?

already_counted.description: Approve final recovered-data package and destination

incremental.description: Maintain validated recovery profiles and repository compatibility

approvals.approved_version: Exact recovered-package hash, provenance log and repository destination approved in s5; changed contents require new approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: five repeated recovery-setup hours saved less two upkeep. Low: bespoke formats and native imports leave no new saving. Evidence-repository commitment retains full effort; no recovery success or computation benefit is counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Review alleged computer crimes, available evidence and investigation authority
Choose investigation hypotheses, evidence priorities and preservation sequence
Write the computer-crime investigation plan and resource sequence
Approve the complete investigation plan against authority and evidence priorities
File the approved investigation plan in the controlled case repository

tasks.design: Use native case-plan templates in {DOCS} with existing evidence identifiers from the forensic-case category of {OTHER}. Keep hypotheses, sequencing and resource choices human; reuse case metadata and file only the approved complete plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case plans repeat authority references, evidence identifiers and standard document sections.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and case metadata can reduce repeated entry while leaving strategy manual.
tasks.still_hard: Early evidence is incomplete and collection can alert subjects or destroy volatile evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a proportionate sequence that tests competing hypotheses without assuming guilt.
tasks.altitude: Less plan formatting; investigation direction and authorization are unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate incident containment with evidence preservation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: controlled investigation templates can reuse case metadata but cannot choose hypotheses or evidence-collection priorities.

assumptions: Boundary is preparing and filing an internal investigation plan, not obtaining external legal authority or executing collection. s4 is technical plan approval within already granted authority. Shares are provisional.

Existing case intake supplies case ID, allegation, authority reference and evidence inventory. s1 verifies applicability and manually resolves missing context; s2 records strategy and constraints within full retained time.

s3 saves only copying existing case identifiers and recurring layout. It retains all writing of case-specific hypotheses, sequence, dependencies and resource choices. Test native templates before any integration.
No notice or external submission is assumed. The final filed plan is bound to s4 approval; altered authority, scope or sequence forces reapproval.
research_questions: Which plan sections can safely reuse existing metadata without obscuring case-specific constraints?

already_counted.description: Accept the final technical plan within existing authority

incremental.description: Maintain plan-template fields and case metadata links

approvals.approved_version: Complete investigation-plan revision, authority reference and case destination approved in s4; edits require reapproval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes five metadata-copying and five filing hours less one upkeep. Low assumes native templates and filing already cover these mechanics, leaving upkeep only. Strategy decisions and case-specific writing retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze digital logs to investigate network intrusion perpetrators.

steps.what: Select authorized log sources and verify time zones and evidence integrity
Normalize timestamps and correlate intrusion events across forensic log sources
Analyze log files to identify perpetrators while testing alternative intrusion explanations
Document attribution findings with event references and alternative explanations
Approve final intrusion attribution findings and evidential limitations
Commit approved intrusion attribution analysis to the forensic case repository

tasks.design: Configure native parser mappings and evidence-linked timelines in the forensic-log-analysis category of {OTHER}. The analyst verifies clock assumptions, assesses alternative attribution explanations and approves the finished analysis before case-record commitment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cross-source review repeats timestamp conversion, event filtering and reference copying.
tasks.enabler_now: Native log parsers and timeline views can handle supported formats while preserving original events.
tasks.still_hard: A device, account or network address does not uniquely identify a perpetrator.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish correlation from attribution and expose uncertainty and contradictory evidence.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive timeline assembly; attribution responsibility stays with the analyst.

reach.task: Trace transformed events to source logs
reach.learn: Immutable source lineage and timestamp semantics

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: forensic log tools support parsers and correlated timelines; these show linked events rather than proving an individual's identity.

assumptions: Boundary is authorized analysis of preserved logs through internal findings, excluding new surveillance, external evidence requests and legal accusation. Parser runtime is not human labour. Shares are provisional.

Log producers supply raw timestamp, source ID, event type, account, available network addresses and event reference. s1 validates source hashes, clock offsets and authorization; missing fields remain unknown rather than inferred.

s2 manually establishes parser and clock mappings and checks samples; remaining time covers unsupported records and correlation checks. Savings apply to repeated normalization and navigation only. s3 retains all attribution reasoning.

s4 reuses event references but writes limitations and alternative explanations manually. Native tooling is tested first, and no model names perpetrators. Approval binds the final report and its evidence snapshot; changed content blocks commitment.
research_questions: Can each timeline event be reproduced from its preserved source without silently resolving uncertain identities?

already_counted.description: Approve final attribution analysis and limitations

incremental.description: Maintain parser mappings and source-lineage regression cases

approvals.approved_version: Final attribution-analysis revision and evidence snapshot approved in s5; changes require renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 12 repeated-normalization, two reference-copying and two filing hours less three upkeep. Low assumes source formats remain unsupported and references need manual entry, leaving filing alone. Attribution reasoning is never accelerated.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use native forensic views for repeated mechanics while preserving evidence and interpretation responsibilities.
role.ambitious_version: Produce reproducible forensic findings with explicit uncertainty and fewer repeated handling steps.
